subject: Business Models
title: Dollar Shave Club's Disruption
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Dollar Shave Club's Disruption.

hook.text: A viral YouTube video with the line 'Our blades are great' turned a startup into a billion-dollar company.

buildup.text: Dollar Shave Club shipped razors monthly for $1. Gillette charged $6 per cartridge at retail stores.

discovery.text: The subscription eliminated the hassle of remembering to buy razors. Convenience was the real product.

twist.text: Unilever bought Dollar Shave Club for $1 billion. Gillette's market share dropped from 70% to 54%.

climax.text: A $1 subscription disrupted an industry dominated by one company for a century. Price and convenience won.

punchline.text: $1 razors by mail destroyed a $6 billion monopoly. Subscriptions disrupt.

quiz.question: How much did Unilever pay for Dollar Shave Club?

details.summary: Dollar Shave Club disrupted Gillette's razor market in 2012 by offering quality razors delivered monthly for as little as one dollar. A viral marketing video and subscription convenience attracted millions of members.
details.whyItMatters: Dollar Shave Club proved that subscription convenience could unseat established consumer goods giants. Its viral launch and billion-dollar acquisition by Unilever became the template for hundreds of direct-to-consumer subscription startups across.
takeaways: Subscription convenience disrupted an industry dominated by retail shelf space
Viral marketing delivered massive customer acquisition at minimal cost
Unilever acquired Dollar Shave Club for one billion dollars in 2016

faq.question: How did Dollar Shave Club compete against Gillette's decades of dominance?
faq.answer: By eliminating retail middlemen and expensive marketing, DSC offered comparable razors at a fraction of the price. The subscription eliminated the chore of remembering to buy razors. A funny viral video generated 12,000 orders in the first 48 hours without traditional advertising spend.

faq.question: What happened to the direct-to-consumer subscription model after Dollar Shave Club?
faq.answer: Hundreds of DTC subscription brands launched across categories from mattresses to vitamins. However, rising customer acquisition costs on Facebook and Google made many unprofitable. The model works best when the product is genuinely replenishable and the subscription provides real convenience.
